Chan Master Jin Baofang of Tiantu Mountain in Hangzhou studied Confucianism in his youth. While composing literary essays with his fellow students, he attained a realization upon seeing peony flowers.
He subsequently received the tonsure under Tanran, who instructed him with the "Mu" (柏樹子) koan. Thereafter, he traveled extensively to consult masters throughout the Chan tradition.

He said to himself, "There is no one anywhere who possesses a hammer of such extraordinary caliber. One evening, while he was walking in meditation in the Buddha Hall at Tianjie, he heard the pop of a lamp-flower, which sounded like a clap of thunder.
He immediately went to visit Taigang and asked, "What is the profound, secret meaning of the West?
Taigang stepped down from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "The West has no meaning. Tell me, what meaning is there here?"
The Master had no reply. Thus, he forgot both sleep and food. One day, while ascending the latrine, he heard a neighboring monk striking the counting-sticks (*shaku*) and making a sound;

suddenly, he attained great enlightenment. He then carried incense and entered the Master’s room. Upon seeing him, Master Gang recognized his potential and bestowed upon him a verse of transmission, saying:
"The Patriarchs have no dharma to transmit; It is inherently possessed by every person. You have received this 'dharma of non-transmission'; Hasten to pass it on to future generations."
Kim Myeong-uk finished recounting the causal conditions and said, "Yi-pung’s forge was strict and his gates were so firmly sealed that not even a breeze could pass through;
were it not for the Elder of Tianmu, he would never have been able to dismantle the household and scatter its possessions. Does anyone in the assembly know this news?
After a long silence, he struck the ground with his staff and descended from the seat.
Jingshan submitted this verse: The great earth, mountains, and rivers suddenly enter the official domain; Pines, waters, moon, and wind do not deceive one another.
One simply desires the source to remain vital and flowing; Why worry that the blue seas of the human world will dry up?
The Cloud Verse on Shimen Gate says: Layered cliffs and magnificent pavilions set off the immortal’s journey; They escort the flying immortals to the highest peak.
With a single footstep, he overturns the cauldron of raw iron; In the spring mountains, flowers bloom and wine fills the towers.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Holding up a flower and smiling was adding branches where there were none; facing the wall to settle the mind was drawing legs upon a snake.
Here in my mountain monastery, there is no Zen to be studied and no Way to be learned. I simply teach each and every one of you to become a Buddha and a Patriarch."
"Do you all still believe this? After a long silence, he struck his knee and said: "The sword is named Gueuqie; the jade comes from Mount Kunlun.

He then ascended the hall and said: "When the branches of the *jiong* tree are severed, every inch is treasure; when the secret treasury is exhausted, every point is gold. Since emerging from the cave..."
Crouching on the tiger’s head and grasping its tail—though there may be thousands and tens of thousands like this, they know only how to discuss military treatises from behind the lines.
If you are one who can leap over the gate, I have thirty blows of my staff for you; take them and depart on your own.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised up the words of Venerable Tianmu Li, saying: "In the extreme cold of late winter, when all the myriad trees are withered and stunted, only the plum blossom possesses its full, refined resonance.
Beyond the wild bridge and flowing stream, beside the thatched cottage and the fence, the mountain monk does not understand the intent of the Eastern Emperor;
he sniffs the cold fragrance three times and stands in the evening sunlight. The Master said: "If you take this as an understanding of the Buddha-dharma, everyone, bring fire!"
"Bring it here to look at. As for this "looking," how thick is the skin on a Han person's face? If you understand it as the petty skills of cicadas or insects, it is said again:

"Beyond the wild bridge and flowing water, beside the thatched cottage and short fence. New Tianmu cannot avoid following like a dog's tail after a fox's fur. This winter is extremely cold; firewood and charcoal are both scarce.
It freezes the legs of the clay ox until they shrink, and the eyebrows of the stone tiger knit together. He turns his body toward the north.
The Dipper faces south; its head emerges beyond the heavens. Who is this "I" of mine?

Addressing the assembly, he raised the question posed by Yuexi: "Why does the Iron Ox sleep at Shaoshi? The Master offered this verse: High renown needs no borrowing; it is proclaimed like jade and gold.
Zi’yu (Mencius) carried his treasures as he traveled through various states; He relied upon the gentlemanly influence of Anren (Xunzi).
A monk came for an audience. The Master said, "Tell me, how many strands of my eyebrows have fallen off? The monk said, "I do not see any at all.
The Master said, "For you who are of such high caliber in the study of the Way, where are your eyes? The monk said, "The heavens, the earth, and the great world are all contained within them.
The Master then gave a shout and sent him out.
Addressing the assembly, he cited the ancient case of Tingjian. When Wuji asked him, "Where do you part from me? Tingjian replied, "At the place where Buddhas and patriarchs cannot reach.
Wuji asked, "Is it permissible for others to come there? Tingjian said, "It is a state of natural ease and unimpeded conditions.
The Master composed a verse on this: By the water’s edge and beneath the trees, his former life; On earthen stools and wooden beds, the flavor is excellent. Suddenly, the desire to return arises.
It was turbulent last night; I have idly entrusted my thoughts as a traveler to the mists and clouds.
On the twenty-fourth day of the second month of winter in the fourteenth year of the Zhengde era, he spoke this gāthā to bid farewell to the assembly.
His body was cremated, yielding countless śarīras of five colors, which were enshrined in a stūpa at his native mountain.
Chan Master Xing of Zutang Monastery in Jinling, successor to Chan Master Tianyuan: Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “A sacred tortoise dragging its tail.
The monk said, “Is it not just this? The Master said, “You fabricated Chan practitioner!”
Dwelling at Changtai, he addressed the assembly: "Changtai is now old and ill; I cannot pour out my heart and soul to offer you long discourses or expansive treatises that might lead you astray.

Nor do I require you to possess broad knowledge or penetrate the public cases (gong'an). Regarding the doubt of your fundamental inquiry, you must immediately press yourself into it with your whole being.
Stand directly on the other side, and even further beyond that, and look back. Only then will you know."
"The worldly industries and means of livelihood all flow from self-nature.

This is still merely "head-talk"—what the ancients called the "donkey tethering stake" or the "sweatshirt against the flesh. Nowadays, in various quarters, people often sit fixed within this very thing;
that the Buddha-dharma is entering its autumn is a sign of this. Under my Longta Gate, one must engage in genuine inquiry.
Awakening must be genuine awakening; to let the time pass in vain is truly to be pitied. Take care.
Chan Master Tungkongsheng of Qixia in Jinling went to visit Chengtian [Temple] but did not find accord there. He then visited Taigang. Taigang asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "From Chengtian. Taigang said, "How long is the nose of Chengtian? He replied, "It is just like yours, Master."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Lotus Sutra says, 'I am the Dharma King; I have mastery over all dharmas. It also says, 'This Dharma abides in its own place; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant.
Old Śākyamuni was much like someone who plugs his ears while stealing a bell. Here at Qixia, the mountain gate is in front and the Buddha Hall is behind;
the kitchen and storehouse are to the left, and the Sangha Hall is to the right. Now tell me: which of these is the eternal?"
"Abiding in the fundamental mark. Let us try to bring forth a message that penetrates through. After a long silence, he said: "Ten thousand miles of drifting clouds have finally vanished;
a single orb of bright moon hangs amidst the misty vines."
Chan Master Nanyue Chunsan Chongjing, a successor of Chan Master Deshan An, ascended the hall and said: "I cite Linji’s address to the assembly: 'You all—'"
"Upon this lump of red flesh, there is a true person of no station who constantly enters and exits the faces of all people.
If you do not recognize him, simply ask the old monk. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the true person of no station?
Linji struck him and said, "The true person of no station—what kind of dried dung-stick is he? The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Linji is much like a donkey."
"Do you wish to see? *Du!* (A shout). After a long silence, he said: 'Fire burning at one end, smoke at both ends; this white-thief is stubbornly difficult to hide.
The tower crumbles through the years in a mountain-demon's cave; as before, the Flower Treasury Sea reaches to the sky.'"
Chan Master Biaozhan of Zhongtian in Western India was a native of Fengxiang. Originally a son of the Confucian elite, he joined the Buddhist order in his youth.
Later, he paid his respects to Wuzhuo of Shuijing An as his teacher and sought out Guxin, with whom he attained spiritual resonance.
Ascending the hall, he said: "This is like a white ox in an open field, its horns towering and its coat gleaming in the blazing sun. It runs off to sleep deep within the Snowy Mountains;
how many times have we entered the grass seeking it, yet failed to find it? Suddenly, it is found—yet its nostrils remain unpinched."
Master Ming of Jingtang at Fahua on Lake Tai, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Tianzhen Shan, addressed the assembly. He raised the case of the novice Gao who visited Yaoshan, to which Yaoshan said:
"You have come," [Yunyan] said. "Yes," he replied. Yunyan said, "It is quite soaked. [Dawu] said, "If there is no drum or flute, why play? Yunyan said, "There is not even leather;
what drum could one beat? Dawu said, "There is not even a drum; what leather could one beat? Mi said, "What a magnificent musical performance! The Master said:
"The father and son of Yaoshan are truly like a phoenix soaring toward the clouds, its wings spreading across the six directions."
Yunyan works his magic upon the drum; Daowu works his magic upon the hide. Looking at it with a direct eye, both are merely playing with their mouths.
If one possesses hands of living mechanism, there is another principle at work.

Chan Master Biezhuan Zong of Mount Song, a dharma successor of Chan Master Dongshan Hui, addressed the assembly: "Dwelling among crags and drinking from mountain streams, I gaze upon the clouds and the sky; there is only the pine wind to accompany my solitude.
With eyes wide awake, I see that the vicissitudes of kalpas have been but a dream; when viewed thus, heaven and earth are but a single autumn hair."
Chan Master Nengren Qiu Yue Cheng of Mount Huagui in Qishui was a successor of Chan Master Yangshan Daowei. A monk asked, "What is the realm of Huagui?"
The Master said, "Five leaves, a thousand lamps, all flourishing. A monk asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm? The Master said, "His two eyebrows tower toward the sky.
A monk asked, "If the entire earth were a single pit of fire, what samādhi would one need to attain so as not to be burned? The Master said:
It is eight *li* from here to Youhe.
Chan Master Bafeng was a dharma heir of Chan Master Yuetan Cheng.
At the beginning of the Tianfu era, he resided at Xichan Monastery in Suzhou; later, he moved to Jianfu Monastery in Xingyang. Zhe... [text fragment]... Zhe.
The questioner asked, "Without falling into the old masters' conceptual traps, I beg the Master to speak quickly.

As soon as the words left his mouth, the Master gave a shout. Zhe said, "This is the functional pivot of the ancients; I further request that you grant me some guidance. The Master shouted twice in succession.

Zhe said, "The profound words of the Patriarchs transcend all achievement and sever all predication. When one of extraordinary caliber arrives, how do you lead them? The Master replied, "The wooden man with his double topknots."
He spoke out without any sense of shame or trepidation. Zhe said, "If that is so, then meeting face-to-face, there is no bowing; each simply displays their own family style.
The Master said, "When Manjusri is dismissed, all news is exhausted; once the melody of the pines and wind has ceased, who is left to play?"
The Master bestowed the verse upon Wuwen Kai, saying: "The Three Barriers of Mount Meng and the leakage from the Eight Peaks—I now extend these to you, behind the Bridge of Eternal Radiance.
He further instructed him, saying: "You should study thoroughly and drink deeply of the 'Drunken' [Hanshan] style to continue my lineage."

At the very end, he addressed the assembly. With great capacity manifest before him, the incoming wind was naturally discerned; the key was struck, the barrier breached, and the target hit as the arrow flew.
"As for the news from before the seven Buddhas, how do you all, venerable practitioners of Zen, realize it? After a long silence, he suddenly passed away.
The Third Patriarch, Chan Master Tianran Rui, because of Xingkong, cited Luyuan’s ascent of the hall:

“The direct meaning from the West—how could it not be difficult to speak of? Is there anyone among the assembly who can say it? Come forward and try to say it. At that time, a monk came forth and bowed;
Luyuan struck him, saying, “What kind of time is this to come out? He then returned to his quarters. You...
"How is it? The Master asked. Baizhang said, "Whom has the Master ever questioned in the past? Baizhang replied, "I do not understand.
The Master made a gesture as if to overturn his meditation seat. Baizhang said, "What is the essential meaning that came from the West?

The Master said, "If you, Brother Bin, were to enter the abbot’s quarters, the Master would not say that I am unable to answer this question. Baizhang said, "This monk deserves a beating; he does not deserve one."
[The Master] struck [the attendant] with his staff. The Master then shook out his sleeves and departed.
Zen Master Qian’an Shimen Huangjing Jizhou Bin ascended the hall and said: "To turn back the head and shift the position, one must truly wear horns and don fur;
call it a water buffalo. Even the thousands of sages and myriad worthies have no place to emerge. [He] drew a circle with his staff.
Yihuai said, "If one can bring forth this very thing, it will not hinder the manifestation of some measure of skillful means.
Shimen Yun said, "Even if you could bring it forth, you would still need to study for another thirty years."
Chan Master Zhaojue Wugaitong first visited Tong Wujie, Bai Guruan, Cheng Yuesi, and Yuexi; he found no resonance with any of them.

Later, he called upon Bafeng, who instructed him to investigate the "phrase with words" and the "phrase without words. After ten days, he attained realization. Following his formal installation, practitioners from all quarters arrived like clouds and water.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Luzu has been facing the wall for years; Bimozhi holds his staff all day long. If you cannot adapt and transform when the occasion arises, you will not be permitted to reach home until the year of the donkey."

Ascending the hall: The Great Way has no front or back; the ultimate principle transcends verbal explanation. If you wish to know where to find rest for the body, it is like the clay ox sleeping at the bottom of the sea.
[This was spoken by] Chan Master Guxi Cheng, a successor in the Dharma lineage.
Chan Master Zongyou of Xizong in Chengdu ascended the hall. Holding his staff horizontally across his chest, he said, "Before one's parents were born, it was only this that was clear.
After one's parents were born, it was only this that was clear. Raising the staff, he said, "Everyone, look! What is this?
It is the sound of a familiar bowl clinking. He then cast the staff down and returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Zhàn of Jì’ān on Jīnshān in Zhuōzhōu addressed the assembly:

"In the past, Língyuán said to Yuànwù, 'Although a monk may possess the potential for insight into the Way, if he does not store it deeply and nourish it thoroughly, its manifestation will inevitably be abrupt and violent.
Not only will this fail to benefit the teachings, but it may even invite calamity and disgrace. When I was first in the assembly of Yuèxī, for ten..."

For three years, I finally integrated this matter into a single whole; only then did it become uninterrupted. Were it not for deep accumulation and mature cultivation before its manifestation, how could there be a "today"?

You who are latecomers in your studies, if you do not deeply accumulate and maturely cultivate yourselves, but instead become self-satisfied with a mere trifle, you will find it ultimately difficult to expand your spiritual faculties to their ultimate subtlety. Furthermore, how could such people ever contribute to the monastic community?
Chan Master Bitian Lang of Sikong was a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Wumen of Longmen. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The moon pierces the bottom of the pool in stillness; the wind passes through the treetops and sways."
Addressing the assembly: This very matter is not an easy one. In the past, while at Dafang, I studied under several masters and questioned them about the fundamental principles of Chan.
There were many monks who had much to say; they could cite public cases and engage in rigorous dialectical inquiry with their mouths flowing like a brook.
I, the mountain monk, presumed that the Buddha-dharma ended there. Yet, upon arriving at Longmen, I was subjected to a single, piercing pressure from him—how wonderful!
It is like a cloth bag filled with water chestnuts; all are exposed at once. O practitioners of the Way!

If you wish to continue the life-line of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, if you wish to clarify the eye of the Way, and if you are able to distinguish the heterodox from the orthodox—these essential points for killing or giving life are not to be mastered through mere routine study and refinement.
Once the conditions and circumstances arise, it naturally passes away and cannot be grasped.
Yu-feng Qian said: "Lately, many students rely too much on their cleverness; they do not understand this kind of practice, nor do they comprehend the principles of the teachings. What a pity!"
Chan Master Dongyan Liang of Jinshan was a successor of Chan Master Xingkong Yue.
One day, while in meditative concentration, he attained realization upon hearing a rooster crow. He composed a verse and presented it to Xingkong, saying: "The dog has no Buddha-nature;

Barefoot and with disheveled hair, it runs about in disorder. When the village assembly breaks up, Zheng San is helped back home. Original text: 性空悅禪師法嗣金山東巖亮禪師。一日定中。聞鷄鳴有省。述偈呈空曰。狗子佛性無有。赤脚髼頭亂走。社散扶歸鄭三。原。
Li Er was intoxicated with wine; he merely laughed and gave his assent.
He ascended the hall and said: "All phenomena are not existent; all phenomena are not non-existent. If you can understand the place of turning, a gourd hangs from the eastern wall."
Chan Master Tie-niu Jian of Yufeng at Shiziyan in Huangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Dayun Xing; while at Dayun, he attained a state of liberation.

He lived in seclusion at Tongshan, abstaining from grain and subsisting solely on *cangzhu* (Atractylodes macrocephala). One day, a fellow practitioner visited him from another peak and secretly instructed him to set fire to his hermitage and invite him to Nan’an.
Before long, he arrived at Bāiyún, where he visited Master Jiàn; thereupon, he settled upon the old foundations of Chan Master Qí’ān and constructed a thatched hut.
Monastics soon gathered like clouds, and it was thus established as a monastery. The Master’s spiritual capacity was profound and subtle.
He employed [this method], yet no one knew of it. Later, he sat peacefully and passed away.
His stupa was erected to the left of the monastery.
[The entry for] Chan Master Wansong Xiaotang Man, a successor of Chan Master Shijing: Having long relied upon Shijing, one day while casually reading Master Yuanwu, he said to Guo Gong...
Fuxian said: "The nature and temperament of human beings are inherently without fixed constancy; they shift daily with the flow of transformation.

Since ancient times, although the rise and fall of the Buddha-dharma has followed a fixed numerical pattern, there has never been a principle of flourishing or decline that was not brought about through instruction and transformation.

In the past, when the various patriarchs of Nanyue in Jiangxi benefited sentient beings, they fanned the wind of sincerity and regulated themselves with purity, clothing themselves in virtue and morality, and instructing others through teaching."
Ritual and righteousness cause students to withdraw their sight and hearing, block depravity, sever cravings, and forget gain;

thus they daily migrate toward goodness and distance themselves from transgression, such that the Way is perfected and virtue is complete without their even realizing it. People today are far inferior to those of antiquity.
Desiring to investigate this Way thoroughly, Shi Jing arrived; the Master asked him, "What is this Way? Shi [Jing] replied:

Shigong struck him across the mouth with his fist. After a long silence, the Master remained still. Shigong asked, "Do you understand? The Master replied, "I do not understand. Shigong said, "What a fine 'I do not understand'!
Before he had finished speaking, he struck another blow. Thereupon, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Chan Master Nanzong Sheng of Jinguoyan Dahuayan Monastery was a successor of Chan Master Wuxiang Zhen. Initially he relied upon Guang’en, and subsequently visited Fushan.
[Zhaozhou] held a water jar and a towel for a long time. One evening, during the sequence of paying homage to the Buddha, Zhongshan asked, "Who is there?

The Master replied, "It is I. Zhongshan asked, "What are you doing? The Master said, "I have come to pay homage to the Buddha. Zhongshan asked, "What did the Buddha say to you? The Master said, "He said nothing.
Zhongshan said, "Have you not bowed your head to the ground? The Master said, "I have bowed my head down every single time. Zhongshan said, "And yet you say he said nothing?"
The Master [Dongshan Liangjie] said, "The Way. At these words, the teacher was suddenly enlightened and said, "I understand! Dongshan asked, "What is it that you understand?
The teacher replied, "To reveal it so clearly! Dongshan then gave a shout. As the teacher was about to offer further words, Dongshan said, "The staff is not in my hand;
I grant you twenty blows. The teacher then departed.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If you see that all marks are not marks, then you see the Tathāgata.

Śākyamuni, from the Tuṣita Heaven, trailed through mud and water as he descended into the imperial palace; he cast off his precious and noble robes to don tattered and soiled garments, and through ascetic practice attained the Way."
The earth shook in six ways, and the heavens rained four kinds of flowers. One might think, "This is indeed the man.

But if one views all marks as being non-marks, then seeing the Tathāgata becomes too distant. Pointing up and down with his whisk, he said: "Heaven is heaven; earth is earth; mountains are mountains; waters are waters.
Now tell me, where is the Tathāgata? Have you not seen it? "In the Five Regions, there is but one..."
A reed and mugwort arrow; it stirs up a million soldiers of China. Had it not been Yunmen executing the true command, one would have nearly mistaken the weight of the scale.
During the Tiānshùn jiǎshēn era, I compiled the Genealogical Chart of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and erected a stele at Huìshàn Jìtán on Mount Sōng.

Before the Great Hall, [is placed] the *Zhengxu Mingjiao Dashi Chuandfa Zhengzong Ji* (Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma by the Great Master Zhengxu Mingjiao), the ancestral dragon for ten thousand generations of the Chan school throughout the world,
compiled by the Dharma-heir of Chan Master Xiuxiu of Jingci Temple.
Chan Master Xueting of Zhaokong Temple in Hangzhou, whose courtesy name was Huanji, was the son of the Gui family of Renhe. He was born in the Bingzi year of the Jingtai era.
Suffering from smallpox and a wind ailment, his two eyes were short-sighted; however, he was moved by a golden deity in a dream who urged him to leave the household life.

His mother and elder brother did not grant their permission. During the Chenghua era, he visited Master Xiuxiu at Xianlin Temple, where they attained spiritual resonance upon their first meeting, and he subsequently left home.
At home, he received the "wordless" discourse. At seventeen, he shaved his head and donned the dyed robes; at twenty-nine, he received full ordination.

At thirty-five, he received the seal of transmission from Master Xiuxiu. Furthermore, for four years he attended upon Xiuxiu at Jingci Monastery. At forty-seven, he began teaching the Dharma at Zhaoking Monastery.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised this case: A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. Fortunately, he encountered this monk;
failing to realize it at the moment of the challenge, he missed his opportunity. To this day, Yunmen continues to block the streets and fill the alleys, with no place to put him away.
Had this monk been able to utter a single word—saying, "I will place him here"—[Yunmen would have had nowhere to go].
It is not permitted. For now, I ask the Master to set it aside. Not only for yourself, but for all time, you will become a person who is free and at ease.
Furthermore, this will press Yunmen so hard that he will be flustered and frantic—having let go, he cannot pick it up;
having picked it up, he cannot let go. Is this not the mark of a true man? Nevertheless, even though Huanchi acts in this way, he is still a man of toil.
"Not a few. Furthermore, tell me: is there still a place for them to be set down? [The Master] speaks on their behalf, saying: "Look at what Yunmen says.

This was the Dharma successor of Chan Master Xingkongjue, the Abbot Nengguan of Yuyuan in Jingzhou. Initially he studied under Zuyuan Hai, and later he relied upon Touzi. One day he asked: "There is..."

The Master said, "One cannot remain where there is no Buddha. How do you abide? The Disciple held up his whisk. The Master said, "Run swiftly past where there is no Buddha. He asked again, "And what then?
The Disciple lowered the whisk and said, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. The Disciple said, "Not clinging to either extreme;
difficult for even the thousand sages to perceive. Let us leave this aside for now. An ancient said: 'Where one hides the body, there are no traces.'"
"At the place where there are no tracks, do not hide your body. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Neither identical nor separate.
The Master asked, "If it is not identical, what is it identical to? If it is not separate, what is it separate from? As the Master was about to respond, the Master struck him.
One day, because a chicken flew by, [Zhaozhou] saw through the Master's point of application.
Addressing the assembly: Last night, the horns of a hare gave rise to the view of Buddha; today, the hair of a tortoise gives rise to the view of Dharma.
I shall condemn them both together and cast them beyond the two Iron Ring Mountains. My brow ridge grapples with the great void, and the great ocean battles the summit of Mount Sumeru.
As for the other kings of wind and lords of water, they must suppress their breath and swallow their voices. Now tell me, does this Venerable Neng have any fault or not?
He sticks out his tongue and says, "Pull!
Chan Master Cherkong Tong of Huanglong Temple on Mount Lu addressed the assembly: "The staff has pierced through the nostrils of Śākyamuni and Maitreya;
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra exert their spiritual transformations, yet even if you look, you cannot see them. This is the gate of Huanglong.
"Down! Is there no one here to pull the wedge from behind the head? Pshaw! You dung-heap, you piss-and-shit-dropper! It was your own misguided application of mind.
During the Wanli era, for the long life of Empress Dowager Cisheng, he was summoned to the Fengtian Gate by imperial decree and granted the Tripitaka.
He enshrined it, and it remains there to this day.
Chan Master Wumen Mingcong of Baoyan in Sanhe, successor to Chan Master Juzu of Nan-zhu, ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, one is wrapped in hemp and paper;
after the fifteenth day, one casts off the head and reveals the face. On the very fifteenth day itself, at midnight before the courtyard, one is bent over."
Sitting on his heels, a hair-tip star appeared right at the door. Striking his head and bumping his forehead, he looked silently.
He addressed the assembly: "The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa. Where, then, do you all void yourselves?"
Addressing the assembly: "At Wangzhou Pavilion, I have already met you. At Wushan Ridge, I have already met you. Before the Sangha Hall, I have already met you.
Today, I do the same. Is there anyone here who has met me? Come forth! A monk stepped forward.
The Master leaned his staff against it and descended from the seat. The second day of the first month of the seventh lunar month, the Ren-shen year of the Zhengde era.
He entered nirvana at the age of sixty-three.

Regarding the Dharma successor of Chan Master Taichu Ren, Chan Master Wuya Shun of Huating, he ascended the hall and said: "The dragon roars in the withered tree; the iron flute has no sound. Treading over and overturning the boat—"
"Quai. [The Master] said, "I thought there was something else. "Venerable Shun," he continued, "you are merely grasping at the wind and catching shadows. Do you believe me?
Twenty years from now, someone will provide proof. Later, twenty years passed, and the Master indeed entered nirvana.
Chan Master Xueyan Qing of Nanyue was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tianmu Xi.
Relying upon Jingbi, he sought the heart-dharma, never daring to treat it lightly. On one occasion, while entering the room for instruction, he was prostrating together with Chan Master Cheng.
As the Master asked, "The three 'nots'—" Qing was about to open his mouth to respond when Jingbi placed his hand over [Qing’s] mouth.
He concealed it. The Master suddenly attained realization. He next visited Tianmu Xiu and Jia Shan Jue. The Master knew that the Dharma is non-dual and sealed [his understanding].
Later, he built a thatched hut beside the Goutou Hermitage.
Addressing the assembly, he cited Master Duànqiáo Lún’s discourse on ascending the hall: "The monastic groves are desolate and quiet;
what little there is, these old veterans from all quarters nowadays, though they may roast a few pieces of dead firewood, each merely warms their own doorsteps.
Yet, alas, they pick here and poke there, blowing horizontally and vertically, until even their own selves are completely blackened. Here in my place, I do not..."
Question: "The large and the small; the dry and the wet—gather them all up and heap them in the furnace. Bury the embers deep so that they remain hidden.
Wait for the season to arrive of its own accord. "O assembly, the season has arrived! [The Master] makes a gesture of fanning the fire with his whisk and says:
"Alas! The smoke and flames press upon one. The Master said: "Exhausting one's own mind to the utmost, one laughs the mouths of others to pieces. Furthermore:
He said, "What a fine topic! It is simply that Guoqing could not bring it forth. Today, I, Master Qing, shall bring it forth for him.
He raised his staff and asked, "Does the assembly see? A monk stepped forward, and the Master said, "If you are not a guest of Longmen, take care not to suffer the loss of your scales.
With his staff, he signaled for the monk to step back and descend from his seat.
Chan Master Dongcang Zhenguo Rufu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yinkonghai.
While traveling to visit Bao Yue, he composed a verse on the road, saying: "The ancient path stretches far and wide, traversed at will;
Lifting my eyes and tripping my feet—how pitiable! I know only that clouds rise from the tip of my staff; I did not realize they were suspended [above me]."
Quand l'eau atteint le sommet, elle s'apaise.
Fǎng Hú was a Dharma successor of the Zen Master Cíhuì;
his Dharma successor was the Zen Master Dòufāng Yǐnfēng Gāo. Dōuyán went to consult him, who instructed him to contemplate the "Mu" (無) koan. One day, [Yǐnfēng] asked him: "Have you yet..."
"Do you remember the living head? Yunyan was about to respond when the Master suddenly struck him in the mouth with his fist. At this, Yunyan attained realization.
Chan Master Taixu Yuan, a successor of Chan Master Moutang Zhao, addressed the assembly: "If you have not yet attained awakening, you must sit coldly upon your meditation cushion for ten years."
For twenty or thirty years, look at the face of your parents before they were born.
Master Guxi Qing of Mount Gui, a successor of Master Jingshan Li, ascended the hall while the assembly was gathered. The Master took up his staff and said, "The vermilion phoenix is about to fly."
Startling the flock like wild ducks and cranes, he immediately took up his staff and descended from his seat.
Longmen Yuan said: "Master Xie ascends this pavilion by chance to gaze afar; boundless depths of melancholy arise within the view."

Chan Master Huangmei Fachang Jin, a successor in the lineage of Chan Master Liaochan Neng, composed a verse on the karmic conditions of the novice’s transmission of words: "Ten thousand *li* of home mountains are a single blade of iron;
The mechanism is profound and secure, not to be leaked. This monk, with his bare face, braved the sharp edge; The staff remains to this day."
Fresh blood flowed.
Chan Master Baozang Tong of Chengdu’s Zhaojue Monastery addressed the assembly, citing the karmic conditions of the moon’s waxing and waning. He offered this verse:

“Holding up the full and the deficient moon to question a master of the Way— The autumn light has intoxicated him until his eyes are blurred. Upon the river, white artemisia and crimson waves surge forth.”
Mistaking reed flowers for snowflakes.
Zen Master Ji’an Zu of Niutou was a dharma successor of Zen Master Tianning Xuan.
Having heard that Donglin had attained enlightenment, he presided over the seats of both the Northern and Southern schools. The Master and Gu...
At Xikong Hermitage, those of like mind came to inquire after the Way; however, because the master’s teaching style was solitary and austere, it was difficult to gain entry.

After entering the inner circle, they proceeded to Tianning Monastery, where teacher and disciple attained a profound spiritual accord. Tianning bestowed upon him a verse, saying: "The mind is equal in measure to the void; The Dharma likewise pervades the void.
Abiding not in the principle of the void— This transmission shall continue our lineage."
Fazhou went for an audience. He was given the "Wordless" (Wuzi) as his koan. One day, while Fazhou was walking through the corridors, he heard the sound of the temple bell from the Buddha Hall.
Suddenly enlightened, he immediately rushed to the abbot’s quarters. Upon seeing him, the Master smiled and said, "You have been robbed. Fazhou replied, "The thief has already been apprehended;
please inspect the stolen goods. The Master asked, "What are the goods? Fazhou shook his sitting mat and said, "A mess! A mess! The Master said, "This..."
"Plundering the void, Han! What a mess you've made! Zhou gave a shout and returned to the assembly.
Zen Master Tiancai Ying of Jingshan, Hangzhou, ascended the hall and said: "Master Mota stirs up waves upon level ground and hammers wooden wedges out of empty space.
He has brought back the lethal poison that strikes people, yet when he returns, he simply says: 'I have personally seen the Treasure [Treasury].'"
[The Master] said, "The Moon! One does not know how many people's eyes it has blinded. It is mute, yet it is fit to be loquacious.
Eastern Yu Chan Master’s Dharma heir, Chan Master Tiantong Xian of Bifeng Temple in Nanjing. Yuzhi went to visit him. The Master ascended the hall and extensively cited ancient worthies.
The kōan: Zhi asked, "How can one avoid falling into the snares of others? The Master struck him with his palm and said, "This is falling—or not falling.
Zhi’s long-held doubts were completely dissolved like ice melting; he bowed in gratitude and returned to the assembly.
The Master was traveling to West Lake. At Zongjing Hall, he ascended the seat and said, "This place is just right for preaching the Dharma.
Zhi, from the side, proclaimed, "The preaching of the Dharma is already finished. The Master then descended from the seat.
Chan Master Daoying Ying of Bifeng in Nanjing was a successor of Chan Master Qian of Dongting. While visiting Dongting, he attained realization upon seeing the shimmering waves of Lake Dongting.
He said to a fellow passenger on the boat, "The Buddha-nature is innate and natural; it is neither born nor extinguished. The Buddha-nature is one's own nature; one's own nature is the Buddha."
As for its nature, one does not calculate whether it exists or does not exist;

it is the solitary manifestation of True Suchness (tathatā). This was like the case of Master Deng Chan of Yiyuan. A monk asked, "When a student seeks instruction from a teacher, the teacher may have them bring up a *huatou* (critical phrase) or have them harbor doubt regarding a *huatou*.
Are these the same or different? The Master said, "The moment the *huatou* is raised, one must immediately harbor doubt. How could it be otherwise?

There are two principles. First, by raising the inquiry with a single thought, the state of doubt immediately manifests. Second, by turning it over and back again, investigating and scrutinizing it with deepening effort until one’s strength is exhausted, one will spontaneously attain realization.
The Master has a work titled *Shiyi ji* (Collection for Dispelling Doubts) which circulates in the world.
Yunqi Zhuhong said: "These few words are most essential. Yet nowadays, many people remain stuck on these two points and fail to reach a resolution;
this is because they have never truly applied themselves to the practice."
Chan Master Dingxin Jiefeng of Yuyang, successor to Chan Master Rou of Baofeng, ascended the hall and spoke. He raised the verse on the World-Honored One’s first birth, saying:
"Gautama was born and immediately startled the multitudes; how can this compare to Yunmen’s direct blow? Everyone says he rose early at the fifth watch of the night, but who knows..."
There was another traveler passing by at night.
Sōan asked the Master, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? How do you understand it? Sōan replied, "In the stillness of the night, I burn cypress wood;
its fragrant smoke reaches to the edge of the moon. The Master approved of this.
Bujiji said, "King Aśoka had a fine opening for a question, but it is a pity he did not pursue it;
thus, he left the tiger’s head and the snake’s tail, causing this monk to merely recognize the act of offering incense and choosing fire, unaware that there was something extraordinary beyond this.
Had I been King Aśoka on that day, when the monk responded in such a manner, I would have immediately seized him and said, 'Not yet!'"
Furthermore, it is said: "If one is a clever monk, like a dragon obtaining water, his transformations are unfathomable;
yet if he stands firmly rooted, he may as well overturn [the world] to its very bottom, ensuring that he cannot rise again until the present day."
Hongji Huan’s verse says: The compassionate mother’s heart is one with her young child’s heart; Her love and pity ultimately serve only to entangle the various shadows.
Had she understood how to break through the barrier from the start, Even a flash of lightning and a roll of thunder would have been submerged in silence.
The assembly gathered for the morning session. The Master said, "Disperse for now; the old monk is weary today. He leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
He ascended the hall again and said, "An ancient worthy said: 'I have a single pivot, held up face-to-face. It is like striking metal and stone; it is like playing the *yunchi* flute.
Were it not for those who know the sound, who could understand this? The ancients presented this matter as if they were ancient emperors recording the clouds."

The "Song of the Wind" is of the highest caliber; its phrasing is remarkably similar [to that of the ancients]. Not only does its heroic spirit overwhelm the observer, but its meaning lies beyond the words themselves.
Few are those who, even upon meeting face-to-face, do not miss the mark.
Chan Master Yaoweng Xiao of Dongta,
Jiaxing, the tenth-generation successor of Chan Master Tianmu Jin of Jing Mountain, went to visit Tianmu. Tianmu said, "You are originally a Buddha, majestic and dignified."
Dadu said, "What is the reason for this? The Master said, "I do not understand birth and death; I beg the Master for instruction.
Muzhou said, "Originally there is no wound; why gouge out flesh? The Master said, "I hope the Abbot will show me compassion. Muzhou lowered his head toward the Master’s quarters.
The Master was startled and said, "Are you trying to cut off people's lifeline? He then tucked incense in his sleeve and entered the room. Muzhou said, "You have already arrived."
In a state free from doubt, what fear can there be of birth and death? Under these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Shimen Yun’s verse says: "Failing to recognize that the Golden Hall is one's own home, one needlessly seeks a livelihood in Luoyang."
Turning over, he shatters the Dragon’s Cave; thus he wins a respite from the wind and rain.
At Tianmu, [the Master] ascends the hall: "The arrow-points meet; it is in vain to rely on intellectual understanding. The simultaneous 'cracking' and 'pecking' depends entirely upon the master."
"Let us set aside for a moment the 'simultaneity of the pecking and the hatching. What is this matter of the arrow-points meeting? The Master came forward to prostrate;
as he rose, he let out a shout. Muzhou also shouted. The Master shouted again twice and returned to the assembly. Muzhou planted his staff upright and descended from the seat.
One day, when the Master returned from outside, Muzhou asked, "Where have you been? The Master said, "To where neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs can go.
Muzhou said, "Just now, there was someone who went to that place. Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Muzhou said, "Why do you not understand?
The Master said, "If I understood, then Buddhas and Patriarchs would have reached it. Muzhou said, "So it is, so it is. Immediately—

The Master’s verse says: “The true nature is fundamentally without nature; The true Dharma is fundamentally without dharma. When one thoroughly understands the nature of non-dharma, Where is there that is not fully penetrated?
Longzhen Yin’s verse says: “Stirring the ice-disk, the pearl rolls on and on; Tugging the golden lock, all is vast and silent.”
Meeting him, they spoke in vain of the words of Vipaśyin; the jade flute was held crosswise, its melody naturally sublime.

Chan Master Guyin Jingqin of Doupeng Peak in Jianning Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Song of Wushan. He left the household life under the guidance of Mount Chishih’s Master. Together with Shi...
When the Master discussed the place where the mind arises as an object of perception, Shishi rebuked him. The Master said, "I have no mind.
Shishi said, "This is your knowing that there is nothing known, and your awareness that there is nothing perceived. At these words, the Master was suddenly liberated from body and mind.
Later, he met Chan Master Jinghuang, who further refined and cleared away his remaining attachments. Upon entering Shu, he passed through Nanyang and attained realization at the Jiming River.

Addressing the assembly: Even if one encounters an opening instruction, it is difficult to realize it all at once. One must rely on a *huatou* (critical phrase) to force open the heart-mind and wisdom.

Through long-term practice, refined through a hundred trials and a thousand temperings—like a hen brooding her eggs with warm breath for a long time—one day, when the proper season arrives, or upon encountering a causal condition that triggers the eyes and mind, one finally attains awakening. As the ancients said: "Each flower has its own..."

Open the season. The orchid in spring and the chrysanthemum in autumn do not share the same path. In all practice of the Way, one should distance oneself from clamor and bustle, sever all external conditions, and stifle miscellaneous thoughts.
Hold up the original koan (hvat-t’o) alone. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down;

whether encountering suffering or joy, adversity or favor—at all times, one must not forget it, but keep it present. With single-minded focus and upright intent, apply yourself with earnest diligence.
Reflect, reflect. Moment after moment, investigate within yourself. Turn back and look at this very one who is able to pursue and question:
what is it? If a person can do thus, they will descend into doubt; as they doubt, they go deeper until they reach the end of the path, where the water runs out and the mountains end;
where the tree falls and the vines wither; where there is no room for deliberation; where the mind is forgotten and objects are severed. Suddenly, the mass of doubt bursts apart.
The flower of the mind blossoms brightly, and great enlightenment manifests before one. One suddenly perceives one's own original Buddha-nature;

this singular radiance is not obtained from without. If one truly attains such a perspective, one must still seek out a master of high realization to resolve the distinction between the heterodox and the orthodox;
one must not rest content with this alone. Only then is it called "entering the gate," and only then is it called "attaining the ground."
Guxue Zhe paid his respects. The verse for the stupa says: The green mountains always walk alone; The waters along the banks have never flowed.
If you wish to understand the meaning of the Westward Journey, Even infants have grown white-haired.

Chan Master Baomingjian of Baiyun at Qian’an was a native of Shu. Having entered the path and received the Dharma from Shoutang, he left the Gorges and traveled extensively through the regions of Xiang and Hu.

During the Zhengde era, he planted his staff at Mount Baiyun in Huanggang; dwelling among the crags and drinking from the mountain streams, students from all quarters gathered there until it eventually became a monastic community.
A monk asked, “What is the student’s own self? The Master said, “Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell;
where there is no Buddha, run swiftly past. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “One palm has five fingers.
The monk asked, “What is it to be among those of Mount Baiyun? The Master said, “Tying three strips of bamboo together; a single-character barrier, traversed both ways.”
He pointed to the moon’s brightness. Having finished presenting the kōan, he said: "A monk who answers in such a manner cannot help but find his footing in the realm of existence and non-existence.
Master Ming, however, was not like this. When [the monk] said, 'I do not understand,' he would have replied to him:"
"You do not understand; I, too, do not understand. If this monk remains as he is—stolid and dull—he would receive a blow across his spine.
Why? Because when acting for others, one must act with thoroughness."

In the second year of the Jiajing era, he traveled to various monasteries at Daqi and Guipeng. On the eleventh month, he arrived at Yuanji and visited the elder master Daohong, with whom he felt a profound spiritual resonance.
One day, as they were parting, he said: "When I came, I did not ascend this mountain; when I depart, I likewise shall not descend from this mountain."
"In the end, how is it? Having spoken these words, he passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa behind the hall.
Chan Master Wumen Kai of Tiancheng was a successor of Chan Master Jianfu Cheng; he was the son of the Leng family of Fengyang. Initially, he visited Jianfu, who showed him a bird.

He attained enlightenment upon hearing the "Kōfuku blowing on the cloth-hair" kōan. He traveled extensively to seek instruction from masters such as Bǎofāng Jìn, Wúxué Cái, Huìtáng Zhì, all of whom rejoiced in the density and continuity of his practice.
Later, he returned to Jiànfú. At Jiànfú, he was interrogated regarding the "Gǔshān’s Holy Arrow" dialogue, whereupon he finally attained a state of total liberation.
During the early Zhengdé era, he resided at Tiānchéng and later at Dàolín. Whenever the Master engaged with practitioners, he would take up his whisk and direct it toward them.
The Master asked a student, "What is it? As the student was about to respond, the Master struck him. When Moran and Guxi went to consult the Master, Moran intended to ask a question;
he first seized the whisk, and only then posed his query. The Master clapped his hands and laughed heartily, then returned to the abbot’s quarters.
He presented a verse to Moe-an, saying: "Speech is silence; silence is speech. Where neither speech nor silence reach, the path of the Buddhas and patriarchs is cut off.
Seizing it from the hair of a tortoise, even the highest peak falls. This 'second moon' of the present age weighs a thousand catties;
I entrust this burden to you, He-pi. Shake up my school and propagate the true pulse. Thereupon, he immediately appointed him to share the seat at Longchi in Xiangyang.
Chan Master Shao of Shimen Foqin, of the lineage of Chan Master Bin of Shimen: A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary matter? The Master said, "A snail swallows a duck.
The monk said, "Is there anything else besides this? The Master said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is the extraordinary matter? The Master said, "A snail swallows a duck."
Case. The Master said: "A snail swallows a duck.

When the mist startled him, the leopard changed its stripes; the monk stood there lost in thought, and the Master immediately shouted at him.

Chan Master Liaozongzhen of Taiping in Shuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Jintai Jue. He went to visit Jintai, who asked: "In the story of Danxia burning the wooden Buddha, what was his intention?"
The Master asked, "Why have you shaved off your beard and mustache? The teacher replied, "Seeking fire, I obtained it with the smoke; carrying water, I returned with the moon.
Thereupon, he was granted certification (in'ga). From beginning to end, the teacher never bathed during the three months of summer, nor did he use a brazier in the severe winter.
At the time of his death, he took leave of his patrons and the various mountain monasteries in advance, and passed away sitting upright.
Chan Master Wansong Huilin of Jingshan in Hangzhou was the son of the Shen family of Renhe in that prefecture.

He paid respects to the Elder Pingshu of Tianmu and received the essential instructions of the mind. Later, while staying at Tongtang in the capital, he heard a monk say that Danxia’s discourse on ascending the hall had brought about great enlightenment.
At that time, Konghuan of Funiu was residing in Guangde; the Master went to Chenjie and subsequently attained the Dharma.
While residing at Jingshan, he one day spoke this verse: "For seventy-six years, my life has been like a drifting weed; upon what could it rely? Fundamentally there is no coming or going;
it merely responds to conditions. He then passed away in silence.
Chan Master Fashou Daoji of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Niutou Zu. He was the son of the Zhang family of Xiushui.

He studied under Ji’an Tongche, who bestowed upon him a verse of transmission, saying: "Dharma after dharma is fundamentally without dharma; now I transmit the dharma that is without dharma. Accept it directly right here."
This very thing is the mind-dharma.
At the beginning of the Jiajing era, while residing at An-yin Temple in Jin-ling, he ascended the hall, raised his whisk, and called to the assembly, saying: "Do you see it?
He then struck once and said: "Do you hear it? Since seeing occurs as soon as it is raised and hearing occurs as soon as it is struck, the wondrous treasury of True Suchness is beyond thought.

This is groundless criticism. You should simply remain cool and detached. It is you yourselves who are not true men; instead, you frequent the gates of others, seeking knowledge and seeking understanding.
You conceal your own family treasures and willingly endure the cold, falsely believing that the sages possess some other extraordinary marvel.
Ryūchin-in said: "An'yō has passed through the silver mountains and iron walls; emerging from the great field of liberation, he directly confronts all who enter.

The Master said, "Layman, do not be attached to words. The Layman replied, "I ask the Master to set aside words and cast a single hexagram line for me to see.
The Master called out, "Wutai! Wutai responded, "Yes? The Master asked, "From where does this single line arise?"
Puming said: "To discuss 'before the lines' and 'after the lines,' or 'existence' and 'non-existence,' is entirely irrelevant to the Great Changes (*Yī Jīng*).
Even if one call and one response were as distinct as the hexagram lines themselves, that still would not make one a true monk.
As for the ultimate point—whether or not the Changes existed before the lines were drawn—why did the old man of Tianning not immediately call out, 'Wutaishan! and wait for the mountain to respond?"
It would have been well had he simply said, "Has there originally been any change? Master Lu’s mouth would surely have had something else to enter upon, sparing us much subsequent circumlocution.
Longxing said, "Everyone, do not be so strange. Longxing will discuss this with you in a straightforward manner.
Lu Gong simply asked, "Is there a message before the drawing, or after? Longxing replied, "If you can realize it before the drawing, you may claim to have met Fuxi.
If you can realize it after the drawing, you may claim to have met Fazhou. If you can realize it at the point where not even a single hexagram-line has yet been cast—"
"Agreed. You have met Master Lu; he has recommended you in its entirety. Before the painting and after the painting, it is all one great volume of the *I Ching*.
From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, it is not separated from daily life—do you still need a recommendation?"
Yulin Xiu’s verse says: A ruined wall and broken house dwell in the secluded forest; From back to front, the gates remain unshut.
Turning north and returning south, they join shadows and echoes; Piteous indeed, a mere few feet separated by a thousand layers.

The first verse of the original collection says: On the dais of the Emperor of the Xī (Fuxi), they spoke of the Master of the Kitchen (Cheng Yao); Before the courtyard of the Master (Confucius), they met Zhongni (Kong Qiu).
They lived together all because they did not know one another; Yet it was he who struck the golden hammer behind the head.
Xiong Nan asked, "Suppose someone were to come with a sword and take the Master's head; would you still try to avoid it?
The Master said, "If there were one who does not blink, then even a general would have no fear of death.
The monk Xiong Nan made a gesture of brandishing a sword, and the Master threw himself down. Xiong Nan said, "What a fine master! You are dead beneath the sword! The Master rose up and scolded him.
He laughed loudly and said, "What? What?
Shi Jingzhai asked, "Is it not the case that all dharmas flow forth from this very place? The Master shouted, "Setting aside all dharmas for a moment, what is 'this very place'?
Jingzhai struck the chair with his fan. The Master said, "Layman, you have indeed reached this place."

Jingyan Buddha Opens His Eyes. Entering the hall, he said: "The Buddha of Nan Temple has his eyes opened; the Buddha of Bei Temple emits light.
If you deliberate upon this as something extraordinary, it is much like seeing ghosts in broad daylight. *Du!* Let us set that matter aside for a moment. As it says in the scriptures, the Buddha..."
The true Dharmakāya is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things, like the moon reflected in water.

it has never been interrupted. Guo said, "Why do I not see it? The Master said, "It is emitting light right now."
Shimen Yun said: "Fazhou was struck by the sound of the bell; his ears were suddenly pierced open, and he realized that his entire being had become supple and alert.

In the autumn of the Gengshen year, his illness became critical. Some urged him to sit up; others requested that he recite a verse.

The Master said, "These are merely literary embellishments, not my concern. With a flicking motion of his hand, he passed away. He was seventy-four years old and had spent fifty-two summers in seated meditation.
Those who received his teachings numbered over a thousand. Among his入室 (入室) disciples were those such as Yuan and Daqin. After his cremation, a stupa [was erected].
His bones were enshrined in a separate chamber facing south; this chamber has now been expanded into the Chan-Yue Hall, while the stupa remains as it was.
Chan Master Miaozhong Xuan of Xingshan Temple on Mount Baitu in Qian’an, a successor of Chan Master Fu Niu Bin, re-established Mount Hu in the early Chenghua period.
