The Master held up his staff and said, "Do you understand? The monk hesitated; the Master struck him.

Chan Master Yuequan Fazhu of Tianchi Monastery in Huzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Bifeng Xian. Born into the Fu family of Jiaxing, he attained awakening upon reading the *Platform Sutra*.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the causes and conditions of time and season.
Just as the midsummer heat gradually increases, from the time Śākyamuni was born until this very day, there has not been the slightest sign of change or alteration.
Since the seasons themselves have undergone no change, you should know that his majestic physical marks and signs likewise possess not even a hair’s breadth of alteration. Without cause, he...

For forty-nine years, he spoke of mind and nature, and of the sudden and the gradual, causing his descendants of later generations who were not "men capable of pecking and hatching" to be entirely drenched with foul water. Now that we have met on this narrow path, it does not matter;
let each of you give him a ladleful. Have you not heard it said: "If you receive an ox from another, return a horse to them"? Sacrifice your own body.
[The Master] bestows the physical body upon them. Who is it that repays this kindness?
[He] strikes the whisk and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day: A sidelong glance casts light like an arrow’s flight; today once again marks the first month.
At every household door, peach-wood talismans are pasted up; Great ghosts and small ghosts all flee and hide away. Yet there remains one who does not obey the cycle of Yin and Yang.
A man of ancient appearance, majestic and imposing. No trace of his presence can be found; he is as dark as ink, more black than lacquer, and as dense as the *yulè* tree.
His eyes cannot be met by even the sharpest gaze. Today, he has been caught and defeated by this mountain monk. I have come specifically to report this news to you all.
*Pah!* In the Buddha Hall, they offer prayers of praise; before the Sangha Hall, the assembly gathers like clouds.
Lu Wutai asked, "Where have the seventeen hundred spiritual teachers of this land gone now?
The Master pointed to a cicada chirping on a tree in the courtyard and said, "There is one here as well. Lu replied, "It makes a sound with its mouth.
The Master said, "To call it 'making a sound' is already to miss the mark."

Jingshan Jin said, "When Yuzhi acts as a teacher in this manner, not only do noble guests see through him, but he has also buried seventeen hundred patriarchs under the trees in his courtyard; to this day, they cannot rise.
If one were to ask New Tianchi, he would say that a staff-blow is like falling rain and a shout is like a rolling thunderclap. Lord Lu must indeed be a noble guest of refined literature."
"Know me, O monk; I have another special quality.
Donglin said, "The two elders established this phrase of guest and host; it blocks the sea and displaces the mountains, causing dragons to race and elephants to flee—all emerge from it.
When Lord Lu asked, "The head cannot be reached," Donglin replied, "It is not so; wait until you ask: 'Where is it now?'"
"Where is Master Shi? he called out in a loud voice. "Mr. Lu! Mr. Lu responded. "I say to you, Mr.

Lu, if you have the leisure, come and travel with this old monk to Mount Jing once. If you can penetrate sound and form, you will recognize that the person beneath the official cap is none other than your former self."
Chan Master Tianranhui of Duoyun once encountered a layman who asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "From where have you come just now? The man replied, "From behind the mountain.
The Master said, "Where are you going? The man replied, "To behind the mountain. The Master said, "I am glad that your coming and going are so clear.
The layman bowed in thanks. Whenever the Master responded to an occasion, he would simply say, "Excellent," or sometimes, "Well-gone."
Chan Master Wugai Bian of Longmen at Jing’an was a successor of Chan Master Guanghui Lian. He went to attend upon Guanghui, who gave him the koan: "The myriad dharmas return to one.
He harbored great doubt about it. One day he heard a monk say: "Having passed through the waves of the three tides, listen attentively for the single roll of thunder. Another monk said: "What..."
"Not saying 'riding a donkey,' one tramples through the waves of Lake Dongting. At these words, the Master suddenly attained realization.
This was Chan Master Kuan of Da Fang in Songzhu, a successor of Chan Master Xin of Yuyang.
When [the student] Wuai Li came to consult him, the Master said: "I do not ask about the seven-day session at Mount Fu Niu."
"How is it with the meditation hall at Zhongnan? Li said, "At Vulture Peak, [the Buddha] struck the seven-day drum; it was nothing but lumps of mud and clods of earth.
At the meditation hall at Zhongnan, he emits great radiance. The Master let out a thunderous shout and asked, "Right now, where is this radiance?
Li was speechless. The Master laughed heartily and said, "So it is, so it is!"
Chan Master Wuqu Ruokong of Jiewei, Jiaxing, was the dharma heir of Chan Master Dongta Xiao, the eleventh-generation successor of Jing Mountain.
He was the son of the Shi family of Xiushui. By nature he was compassionate and benevolent, and he devoted his mind to [the Way].

In the Inner Canon, he was like a fellow traveler on the boat of the Dharma. For eight years he lingered there, visiting Master Yeweng at the Eastern Pagoda. Whenever he presented his insights, the Master would sweep them away.
One day, the Master said to him: "The First Patriarch came from the West to point directly to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature, one becomes a Buddha."
"It lies solely in directly realizing it within yourself. If you can believe this, you may let go of all external conditions and investigate: 'To what place does this one thing return?
" The Master understood the meaning. Later, upon hearing a rooster crow, he attained awakening and immediately shaved his head to become a monk.
Shimen’s Cloud Verse says: Dreaming I ride a crane with a beak of gold to ascend the golden palace gates; A cluster of immortal breezes stirs from my two flanks.
Just as the cold cock of the inn cries out at dawn, The golden sun pecks through the kingdom of lapis lazuli.
Kim Myeong-uk’s verse says: The light green waters flow gently as the spring days grow warm; The immortal boat drifts everywhere, then he mounts his steed again.
The road is endless as it passes before his eyes; He reins in his horse and returns as the moon turns westward.
A Verse on the Abundance of Micro-dust: Three times he attempts to pass through the surging waves of Yu’s Gate; His body remains amidst the vast billows, separated by a great distance.
Only when the spring breeze opens a single thread does he emerge; Holding his head high and bearing his horns, he soars straight into the midnight sky.
The Wild Old Man handed over the verse of the Master’s Dharma, saying: "Neither dharma nor non-dharma; neither nature nor non-nature; neither mind nor non-mind.
The transmission of the Dharma of the mind to you is complete."

Closing the Gate to Address the Assembly: For over thirty years, I have engaged in inquiry and practice. When asked about the Dharma by masters of the school, I have always said there is nothing to speak of;
when asked about the Buddha, I have always said he is without form. Fortunately, having attained this state of no-form and no-speech, I suddenly realized that all my skillful arts were broken.

With the staff of the master, I struck at the two empty hands and entered the Mysterious Barrier. Sitting and watching the waxing and waning of yin and yang, I spoke this verse: "The impoverished son returns home. Long... [The text ends here].

This is the dwelling. Good Wealth has traversed the entire Forest of Miscellaneous Flowers; the great chiliocosm is gathered within the tip of a single hair. Pushing open the mouth of emptiness, he covers the upper gate.
Opening the lock, he seals the profound barrier himself and buries himself alive. "I myself close it; I myself open it. With a single blow of the fist, he shatters it.
The pivot of the dark gate releases this man from before.

When the assembly had gathered for the ascent to the hall, the Master remained silent for a long while, then let out a shout and said, "Calamity arises from within one's own house. He then returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Today is a fine festival, the seventh day of the seventh month. Gather all your wiles within yourself to come and eat.
Swallow this exquisite and marvelous skill all at once; exhaust it completely without leaving even a trace. In the past, you played with cleverness and lost your true nature;

from now on, embrace simplicity and maintain your honest ignorance. Soaring on clouds and riding on mists—all shall become empty. A hundred clever tricks are not equal to one moment of sincerity. How so?
This is one sentence of plain truth. Two is two; one is one. A fresh clearing after the rain:
when the long rains have finally ceased, all people rejoice. Green willows dance in the warm breeze; yellow orioles sing without ceasing.
The pivot of the patriarchs of ten thousand ages has all been leaked at once. If you can comprehend it directly, it remains as before—there is no connection.
Why? Because one morning the tree falls and the oriole does not come; do not mistake a tortoise for a turtle.

The plum rains; the plum winds blow gently; the plum rains fall in fine drizzle. At the summit of Mount Sumeru, the fragrant waters scorch the forehead; upon the ocean surface, the waves knit their brows.
In the ponds, the frogs beat their drums with a sound like thunder. If you can grasp the meaning of the Westward Journey at this moment, you will realize it here and now.
Only then do you know that every person is the Fifth Patriarch, and that everywhere is the Great Gate of Liberation of Huangmei;

it originally has no lock or key, for the ground of ultimate reality is fundamentally level and even. If you have not yet clarified this, then no matter how many times you refine yourself through cultivation, it will be in vain and merely a source of toil.
Why? It is simply because you seek Huangmei at the edge of your eyes and the corner of your ears, and thus you continue to cast away your own ancestral heritage.
Tian-di. Addressing the assembly: "If you can realize it before words, you are already at the edge of the world; if you take it up after the phrase, the path grows ever more remote.
With one blow, the Iron Ring Mountains shatter like dust; the sea and sky are vast and wide, and the geese fly in a slanting line."
New Year’s Eve. When time is exhausted, how can it be compared to when the days are exhausted? If the months are exhausted, the same will be true for the coming year.

Having passed through thirty-six weeks, Old Wang of the Eastern Village burns paper money at night. This old fellow possesses not a single thing, yet he responds to the conditions of this particular season.
He picks up his staff and says: "There is only this; it is inexhaustible and endless. Through kalpas and years, tonight..."
He sent it off at the appropriate moment to avoid being entangled in verbal complications. Throwing it down, he said: "That which was acquired over kalpas is now brought to an end;
with both hands empty, he receives the New Year."
The Lantern Festival. Amidst the sound of painted horns, to claim one has realized Avalokiteśvara is not yet to be considered a master.

Within the shadows of the colored lanterns, to know how to return to Śrī is merely to boast of being a skilled hand. To report it in such a manner to all people would surely cause the void to burst into laughter.
If you Chan practitioners have still not glimpsed it, then look again at the Ao Mountain as it runs headlong upside down.
Addressing the assembly: Before the vast chaos had yet been distinguished and heaven and earth had not yet separated, there was already a single thing.

People of this age call it the "Treasury of the True Dharma Eye," and it is also named the "Sublime Mind of Nirvana. It is now present at the gates of your six sense faculties, manifest and clearly evident within the four modes of deportment.
[The Master] picks up his whisk and says: "Do you see it? If you see it, you will penetrate this message."
The Lecturer enters. The Master asks: "The first phrase before the sutra fills the void; the last phrase after the sutra pervades heaven and earth;
the phrase that encompasses them all covers the universe. At such a moment as this, where would you open your mouth?
The Lecturer has no reply.
Wu-huan was mending a tent when the Master arrived and swept the ground. He asked, "What are you doing? Wu-huan replied, "Mending a tent.
The Master said, "Whose tent do you need to mend? Wu-huan said, "Master, why do you trouble people so much? The Master then struck him.
Wu-huan made a gesture of sweeping the ground, and the Master took up the broom and left.
Yu Juzhen came to pay his respects. The Master said, “I hear that while at Tianxin Academy, you attained some measure of realization;
is this so? Yu replied, “It is. The Master asked, “What is this ‘measure’? Yu said, “It lies in the very moment the Master opens his mouth.
The Master said, “That has nothing to do with you. Yu stepped forward and clapped his hands. The Master said, “This is merely what you learned in the academy. Yu—[remained silent].

He withdrew and returned to his place. The Master said, "You have seen but one spot. Yu said, "This is that which I do not forget in my daily life. The Master said, "That will only serve for your use while on the road.

Yu then presented a verse on the theme of "A Life amidst Clouds and Water Filling the Sky": *Clouds disperse and waters dry up;* *Where does life reside then?* Yu hesitated. The Master snapped his fingers once and said: [The verse: *When clouds disperse and waters run dry,* *Where is the livelihood?

The entire sky is vast;* *In the midst of the great void, there is no trace;* *Only the wind and moon remain as companions.* The Master said, "When clouds disperse and waters are exhausted, where is your livelihood? Yu was about to offer a response when the Master snapped his fingers once and said: [implying the end of the exchange].
While staying here, Yu attained a realization regarding this.
Shimen Yun said, "In this Tiantai Academy, how many scholarly youths of refined talent dwell within!"

With radiant wind and clear moon, he extensively extols the sublime Way. Without cause, he encounters clouds and rain filling the sky, causing those of obscured minds to long for the Golden Horse Gate and walk the streets of Chang’an—much like one gazing toward the imperial capital from a distance of only a few inches.

If it were a thousand li away, upon merely inquiring at Shimen, the clouds would disperse and the waters would dry up. If you intend to deliberate, I shall suddenly strike you across the face; take this well to heart. Heaven!
At the bottom of the Heart Study Hall, all were completely liberated.
While walking by the lake under the moon, Wuhuan arrived. The Master said: "The bright moon and the clear breeze; the water and the sky are one and the same color."
"Everyone is within this very thing, yet none can emerge from it. Huanchu said, "Why do you 'beat the grass to startle the snake'?
The Master asked, "And what about you? Huanchu said, "Look beneath your feet. The Master laughed heartily and then departed.
While the Master and Wuhuan were walking together, they heard the sound of wind rustling through the *chala* trees. The Master said, "When the wind comes to this tree, it roars like a lion;
when the wind ceases, it enters nirvana. Wuhuan asked, "When the tree falls and the wind subsides, where is the lion roaring?
The Master remained silent for a long while. Wuhuan said, "That 'great roar' is not the roar of a lion. The Master then struck him with his palm.
Tie Rongxuan’s eulogy says: The young lord invites his companion to roam atop the tower where the moon is full; A beautiful lady further modulates her song of the "Yizhou" melody.
She raises a spring breeze right upon the banquet table, Carrying it all the way to the very end of the waters of the Xiao and Xiang rivers.

Lu Wutai raised a case where a monk asked: "Jiashan acknowledged that you, Master, had said, 'I have lived on this mountain for two thousand years and have never once mentioned a matter of the Zen school.
When it came to the occasion of packing his bags to depart, he said, 'This monk [will] overturn the bed. Lu Wutai then said, "Before this monk, [Jiashan] overturned the bed."
Later, when the monk departed, he was at a loss for a single word. "Could you, Master, provide a substitute for him? Could you offer a turning phrase?

The Master said, "These two are men who have heads but no tails. When the monk asked this of Jia Shan, Jia Shan replied, "I have never said such a thing before," and he immediately called his attendant to expel the monk.
Thus, he did not fail to possess the beginning but lacked the end; it was like a thief passing by while the householder is away.
The monk went to where the monk from Mount Jiangshan had raised the koan the previous day. He then punched the air twice and gave it a shove, saying, "It is buried.
He thus avoided being defeated in battle and forced to retreat. [Jiangshan] said, "Is that so? The Master said, "Tell me, did this monk bury himself, or did he bury Jiangshan?
[Jiangshan] said, "Both are buried. The Master said, "Be careful not to implicate me. Lu laughed heartily.
The Master said, "Go! Lu said, "Wondrous! Wondrous!
Longxing Zai remarked, "A master of the ancestral school; Tianran is still present in the imperial court. A noble guest has happened to meet us today;
with hearts beating as one, we tie the mandarin ducks together, until the seat is divided at Cangwu and the music resounds with a grand flourish."
If, on that day, Jia Shan had exerted his utmost effort, the dharma-lineage of today’s Master Lu would not have fallen into such desolation;
yet, though he drew his sword to come to the aid [of his teacher], he was instead seen through by the secular official.
In the second month of winter in the Jīmǎ year of the Wànlì era, having completed the transmission of the Dharma to Wúhuàn, he said to him:
"Next year, during the Mid-Autumn Festival, within five or six days, I wish to depart; you should come. When the appointed time arrived, the Master manifested a slight ailment and spoke this verse:
Birth and death are but empty flowers; passing from death to birth is a single dream. This skin-sack is entrusted to the fire god (Bingding Gong);
the white bones form a broken bridge. Along with the assembly, we laugh aloud: under the bright moon and clear breeze, we sing and play.
Furong Daokai said: "Since this skin-sack has been entrusted to the element of fire, these white bones shall all return to the Broken Bridge.

Ultimately, with what will you enjoy the breeze and play with the moon? After a long silence, he said: "Because I see the mist and clouds rising from behind my back, I know the stars and moon circle the eaves and rafters."
Shimen Yun took his leave of Furi. Entrusting his skin-sack to Bing and Ding, his white bones returned to Duanqiao. "In the end, what will you use to play with?
After a long silence, he said: "The vast autumn sky; the solitary wild goose and the setting clouds."
Master Huimù’s secret verse says: "Ever since treading upon the frost of the wooden bridge, The rooster's cry at the thatched inn has lingered through the long midnight.
As the pestles and mortars strike again with increasing urgency, The traveler finally need not expend further deliberation."
The Master was born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month in the Xinhai year of the Hongzhi era. He passed away on the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the Gengchen year of the Wanli era.
His worldly lifespan was ninety years; his stūpa is located at Ben’an.
Chan Master Daixiu Zonglong of Seven-Pointed Peak in Suizhou was a successor of Chan Master Haichan of Shimen. He was the son of the Jia family from Yidu in Qingzhou.

One day, while carrying water, he accidentally struck a wall and attained realization. He composed a verse, saying: "The nature and essence of the great earth, mountains, and rivers are empty; how can one distinguish..."
Wandering east and west, he happened upon a verse of selfless truth: "Ten thousand rivers and a thousand mountains are all one.
He visited Wujin at Qianming Temple in Henan, where their karmic conditions harmonized and he received formal certification of his realization.
In his quarters, he would occasionally suspend three "gateless barriers" (san guan yu) to test his students.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "Yellow gourd, eggplant. The monk did not realize it.
He arrived at a hermitage. The master of the hermitage asked, "Where have you come from, Venerable? The monk replied, "From Seven-Pointed Peak. The master asked, "What words were spoken there?
The monk said, "I asked about the meaning of the Westward Transmission, and the Master [there] teased me. The master said, "Try to recount it for me. The monk related the previous conversation.
The master prepared incense and bowed from afar, saying, "The Great Rest Ancient Buddha has emitted his light. At that moment, the monk...
Wu. On the eighth day of the eleventh month in the twenty-first year of the Jiajing era, he gathered the assembly and wrote this verse:
"Holding the three periods of time as my staff, The ten directions are originally my old cassock. The clay ox and stone tiger know the news; I have trampled through emptiness."
Kong returned home and, placing his writing brush down, sat upright and passed away. He was interred at Mount Doufeng.

Zen Master Tianzhen Daojue of Mount Doufeng in Jianning Prefecture was a successor of Zen Master Qin of Mount Doufeng. Upon contemplating the phrase "All phenomena return to One," he attained awakening and composed this verse:
He said: "With one hand clapping and one hand drumming, the Unranked True Person performs a dance beyond the ordinary. From his mouth he sings a tuneless song;
the three thousand Buddhas share the same mother. He went forward to present this ancient sound, and the Master approved it.

He struck him again. The Master said, "Gold and brass are not distinguished; jade and stone are not differentiated. Guo laughed heartily and left the Dharma Hall.
One day, because a monk recited a verse on wind-bells: "Copper lips and iron tongues, too sharp and new;

Hung from the corner of the tower, they count no spring. Beyond words are hundreds of thousands of samādhi-dharmas; Through the wind, they are spoken to those who truly understand. The Master attained realization and presented it to him.
Jue. Jue approved of this.
Longmen’s *Xing Song* says: "It is not the spots of a man, but the stripes of a tiger; Twice its fangs and claws are revealed, towering and jagged.
If you now wish to see Old Zhaozhou, Every刹 (dust-mote world) and every 塵 (particle) speaks with a broom."
The *Duo-song* (Bell-Eulogy) for Protecting the Nation says: Her lotus-leaf skirt is cut in one pattern; Her willow-blossom smile opens on both sides.
She enters straight to the heart of the pond and cannot be seen; Yet by her singing voice, someone must surely be coming.

Chan Master Ji Zhou Hong of Nengren Temple on Mount Huagui in Xichuan was a successor of Chan Master Ding of Xilin. A native of Sangluo in Jiujiang, he took the Fourth Patriarch Jie Wen as his teacher.
One day, while escorting a deceased monk, he was moved to sever all worldly ties and went to study under Xilin. Xilin instructed him to contemplate the Three [Mysteries].

One day a monk came for an audience. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Huangbo. The Master asked, "What words or phrases did Huangbo say?"

The Master asked, 'How many people understand this? [Zhaozhou] replied, 'Changchun and Dajue. The Master asked, 'What about you, Senior Monk? [Zhaozhou] replied, 'I do not understand.'"
The Master said, "Do you truly not understand? He replied, "Truly, truly I do not understand. The Master said, "Return quickly tomorrow; he will surely explain it for you as the Head Seat.
The monk took his leave and returned to Huangbo. Indeed, upon hearing these words, he attained realization.
The Benevolent One (the Master) was once asked: "Two yellow orioles sing among the verdant willows; a flight of white swallows soars into the blue sky.
During the Mid-Autumn Festival in the year of Xinchou of the Wanli era, as the Master gazed at the moon, he pointed to it and said to Anxin, "When it is dark, I shall depart.
On the thirtieth day, he bathed and passed away while seated. His stupa was erected to the west of the temple.
Chan Master Yungu Fahui of Xushan, Jiaxing, was a successor of Chan Master Tianning Ji.
He was the son of the Huai family from Jiashan. Having studied under Master Fazhou, Fazhou instructed him to contemplate the phrase "Buddha-recitation.

[The Record of Great Enlightenment]. Master Zhou specifically composed the *Linji Twenty-Seven Generations Source and Lineage* and transmitted it to him.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Where there is water, there is moon; where there is no mountain, there is no cloud.
The monk asked, "Is there nothing more extraordinary than this? The Master said, "Do not mistake a tortoise for a turtle."
Hanshan Qing traveled north. The Master presented him with his robes and a verse, entrusting him with these words: "My Great Dharma rests upon your shoulders;
be careful not to treat it lightly. You must cherish it. Hanshan responded with respectful assent and bowed to receive them.

The Master’s passing left behind a great radiance that extends into future generations. His stupa was erected to the west of Qizhen Temple, and the inscription for the stele was composed by Yuan Liaofan.
(According to the *Stupa Inscription for Master Qing* written by the public figure Qian Moucai, its concluding remarks state in brief: "However, my Great Master’s succession... )
The pulse lies in the source. According to the Master’s own account, he attained the fundamental core of Yungu;

through deep investigation and diligent study, he reached the point where he struck upon the phrase, "The whirlwind strikes and the mountain crumbles," at which time his mass of doubt was washed away. At that moment, there was a verse regarding the nostrils pointing downward.
As for the discourse on the iron ox entering the water, it was likely through this that [the Master] attained awakening; thus, he engaged in many separate inquiries.

He had no one to whom he could claim succession, yet his realization under Master Gu (Yunju) was so profound that he still spoke of his indebtedness to the Dharma. Judging by this, the Master was originally without doubt at Yungu.
If one traces the lineage from Yungu through Fazhou and Jizuo back to Great Master Linji, then the Master’s succession would be the twenty-eighth generation.

Nevertheless, regarding the profound principles of the Dharma and the application of its skillful means, one must truly penetrate the five schools (*pañca-nikāya*). These function spontaneously and do not stand as fixed entities;
they are by no means the mere preservation of a single, stagnant lineage. Why is this? Though the branches diverge from the source, nothing can surpass what followed after Caoxi (Huineng).
When the five schools flourished excessively, they declined at the beginning of the prosperous era. The sword has long since departed; to mark the boat’s position and search for it is surely futile.
To imitate him is merely to seize a dead snake; how could one possibly have the power to rescue this Way?

Dieru said: "In this world, those who snatch at goods and plunder the market are despised and laughed at by the wise. How much more so regarding the editing and transmission of the *Zongcheng* (the Vehicle of the Lineage), where the very life-force of wisdom is at stake!
Thus, there are those with firm evidence, such as Donglin Wu and Tianning Xuan, who emerged from the depths of Bafeng."
Xuanchu transmitted it to Ji’an Zu; Zu transmitted it to Tianning Ji; Ji transmitted it to Yungu Hui; and Hui transmitted it to Hanshan Deqing.
This succession of masters and disciples, this transmission from patriarch to patriarch, is something understood by everyone from young children to white-haired elders.

Recently, however, I have seen that in the *Continued Lamp of Shaolin*, [the lineage] has been compiled as descending from Dajian Run. This is intended to open up a source of dispute between the Heavenly King and the Heavenly Emperor for future generations.
Furthermore, the *Nanjian Xudeng Cungao* (Supplementary Lamp Records from Nanjian) is truly the embroidered history of the Chan school and a golden mirror of the Dharma gate;

it is also seen to have been included [in the canon], though the details remain unclear. Because the *Shaolin Shu* appeared earlier and the *Cungao* circulated later, I have provisionally preserved it to await those who possess the true Dharma-eye.
It is like Zhang Wujin pointing out the "Vajra Eye" of Zantang; as for his descendants... [they] are without [fault].
To know one's own ancestral origins is like learning to walk by following the example of Handan; it will surely cause those who understand to look upon it with disdain and laughter.

I have examined in detail how, after Master Qing returned south, he encountered the passing away of his teacher and subsequently established a stupa courtyard. He solicited land to ensure the perpetual maintenance of the stupa.
Master Qing then erected a spirit tablet for his teacher; was this not called "The Spirit Tablet of Chan Master Yungu Hui, the Original Teacher Mingyuan"?

The Dharma-disciple Deqing of Bangle established [the lineage]. Furthermore, regarding the source of the teachings as recorded in the *Zilin Zhanyu Heng Gong Ji*, Qian Muqiai composed the "Epitaph for Master Qing," which includes the words of Master Qing’s legitimate successor, Yungu. It was because Master Qing did not immediately ascend to the rank of Patriarch; he merely offered incense and brought forth [the lineage], which allowed those who were outsiders to act recklessly.

Zen Master Dongxi Fangze of Jingyan Temple in Jiaxing was the son of the Ren family of Jiasan. He studied under Fazhou.

One day, when Fazhou raised the dialogue between Longtan and Tianhuang, [Fangze] reached the point where Longtan asked, "At what place do you not point to the heart-essence? and attained realization. Heaven... [text fragment].
It would be better to untie the ritual restrictions and take up the whisk. Although the Buddha-dharma pervades all worlds, it has never leaked out even in the slightest degree;
how can it be tied? Although it has never leaked out even in the slightest degree, it has likewise never been hidden away even in the slightest degree;
how can it be untied? Thus we know that the Great Master Baizhang, for the sake of beginners, employed this skillful means as a pedagogical device.
These are merely empty words; in reality, they can neither be tied nor untied.

Suppose a man as bold as Meng Babang were to come forth and say, "I can tie what Master Baizhang could not tie," thereby decisively cutting it off so that the monks of the world would lose their bearings and find no way out; he would likewise be able to untie what Master Baizhang could not untie.
This is the place. With a single stroke of understanding, he completely unravels it, leaving the patch-robed monks of the world in total disarray, with no place to hide—how truly extraordinary!
"Venerable elders, since they are men of such stature, why should I not be so? After a long pause, he strikes the whisk once and says: "HŪṂ!"

Chan Master Funiu Wuai Mingli was a successor of Chan Master Songzhu Kuan.

During this time, he uttered the phrase: "With one sound, empty space shatters; the Dharma-King alone is revealed. Later, together with...

Dayuan Yuean entered Zhongnan Mountain. One day, while at the hermitage, he brought up the words of Gaofeng: "A silver mountain, an iron wall. The Master attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse, saying:

"A single awakening and the mind is empty; doubt is instantly dispelled. Picking it up and letting it go, one is naturally carefree. Carrying water and hauling firewood, the whole body is fully manifest.
The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms are all encompassed within the single nature. He further said: "The wondrous essence is suchness, fundamentally self-so..."
Emptiness. There is not a single thing further to be sought. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, waves surge and roll; the sun never departs from heaven and earth.

Having traveled far to seek realization, he was finally granted this verse, which says: "I entrust to you the golden robe to widely benefit all beings. With one shake of the school of Emptiness, the seas and rivers are cleared.
Your nature encompasses the myriad phenomena, revered by humans and devas; Within the gate of Buddhas and Patriarchs, you shall unfold the mechanism of transformation."

Chan Master Wuhuan Xingchong of Mount Jing in Hangzhou, whose courtesy name was Guzhan, was the son of the Zhang family of Xiushui.
His mother’s surname was Bu. On the evening of the master’s birth, she dreamed that a rooster on a bridge flew up into the heavens; consequently, he was named Qiaoying.
At that time, whenever he cried incessantly, it would stop only when ritual implements were arrayed before him. In his early years, he led a group of children with tiles and stones.

He constructed a hall and an image for them and paid homage to them with prostrations. Having brought his wife inside to raise their child, he once sighed, lamenting how deeply entrenched the afflictions of worldly toil were;

how could one escape from them? Hearing that Wuqu was a man of the Way in his true essence, he went to visit him with joy. Wuqu instructed him on the principle of the "special transmission outside the teachings," and he attained a realization.
He subsequently shaved his head, took the precepts, and built a hermitage at Mount Jing. He compiled the sayings of Wuqu, and upon meeting Wuqu again, Wuqu—
Xuefeng said, "What have you been doing? The Master replied, "I have bought a plot of land and obtained the original deed;

Xuefeng threw down the collection of texts, and the Master immediately departed.
Longxing said: "One person has a talisman suspended behind his elbow; another has Mahesvara standing upright upon his crown.
Both are masters of their craft, resplendent throughout antiquity and the present. Yet, if one wishes to be a true descendant of Linji, they still fall short. Why?
Because to emerge victorious from the midst of the fray, one must rely on a lion’s cub."
The Song on the Nature of Longmen says: When meeting, each displays their own family style; The ancestral legacy is inexhaustible for descendants.
The boundless great ocean provides sustenance for leaping carp; The ten-thousand-mile long sky allows the wild geese to soar.
Kim Myeong-uk’s verse says: The momentum for soaring has long been held at the Dragon Gate; With a mere gust of wind and thunder, it chases the evening tide.
Startled, the clay ox breaks forth through the azure sea; A single turn and a sudden thrust, it charges straight into the clouds.
Shimen’s Verse on the Clouds says: "Borrowing my mother-in-law’s robe to greet her on her birthday, His dignified bearing flows forth spontaneously.
There is yet another aspect of his purity: On the imperial street, he conceals his sleeves before the bright moon."
Whisking breezes of spring sway the very axis of the earth; Deep, heavy night rains wash the roots of heaven. Ten thousand layers of silver waves aid the leaping of scales;
With fins beating against the clouds, the seas and mountains grow dark.
“Do not ask aimlessly. Penetrate to the very bone and marrow and speak one phrase. The Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials are beyond all obstruction and protection.
